source_text: Ταῦτα εἰδὼς καὶ πρὸς νόσους ἰσχυρὰν κατασκεύαζε τὴν ψυχήν, εὐθάρσησον ὥσπερ τις ἀνὴρ ἐν σταδίοις ἄριστος ἀτρέπτῳ τῇ δυνάμει τοὺς πόνους ὑφίστασθαι. μηδὲ ὑπὸ λύπης πάνυ πιέζου τὴν ψυχήν, εἴτε νόσος ἐπικειμένη βαρύνει εἴτε ἄλλο τι συμπίπτει δυσχερές, ἀλλὰ γενναίως ἀνθίστα τοῖς πόνοις τὸ νόημα, χάριτας ἀνάγων θεῷ καὶ ἐν μέσοις τοῖς ἐπιπόνοις πράγμασι ἅτε δὴ σοφώτερά τε ἀνθρώπων φρονοῦντι καὶ ἅπερ οὐ δυνατὸν οὐδὲ ῥᾴδιον ἀνθρώποις εὑρεῖν. ἐλέει δὲ κακουμένους, καὶ τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ βοήθειαν ἐπ’ ἀνθρώποις αἰτοῦ· ἐπινεύσει γὰρ αἰτοῦντι τῷ φίλῳ τὴν χάριν, καὶ τοῖς κακουμένοις ἐπικουρίαν παρέξει, τὴν αὑτοῦ δύναμιν γνώριμον ἀνθρώποις καθιστάναι βουλόμενος, ὡς ἂν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἐλθόντες ἐπὶ θεὸν ἀνίωσιν καὶ τῆς αἰωνίου μακαριότητος ἀπολαύσωσιν, ἐπειδὰν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸς παραγένηται ἀγαθὰ τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀποκαθιστῶν.
thought_title: Facing sickness with a strong soul and praying for the afflicted
orientation: Clement is concluding his moral instruction to the newly baptized, telling them how to face sickness and hardship and how to pray for those who suffer.
pass_a_gloss: Knowing these things, also prepare your soul to be strong against sicknesses; take courage, like some man in the stadiums, best, with unbending power, to undergo the labors. And do not press your soul very much under grief, whether an oncoming sickness weighs it down or some other difficult thing befalls, but nobly oppose your thought to the labors, offering thanks to God even in the midst of painful affairs, since indeed he thinks things wiser than humans and things which it is not possible nor easy for humans to find. And have mercy on those who are afflicted, and ask for the help from God upon humans; for he will nod assent to the friend who asks for the favor, and he will provide assistance to the afflicted, wishing to make his own power known to humans, so that, coming to knowledge, they may go up to God and enjoy the eternal blessedness, whenever the Son of God arrives, restoring good things to his own people.

lemmas.gloss: take courage, be of good cheer

choices.english: prepare your soul to be strong
choices.why: The adjective ἰσχυράν is predicative with κατασκεύαζε, expressing the result of the preparation; 'make your soul strong' would also work, but 'prepare to be strong' keeps the verbal force of κατασκευάζω.

choices.term: ὥσπερ τις ἀνὴρ ἐν σταδίοις ἄριστος
choices.english: like some man in the stadiums, best
choices.why: The phrase evokes an athletic contestant; 'stadiums' (plural) reflects the Greek plural σταδίοις, and 'best' renders ἄριστος as a predicate adjective describing the man's excellence.
rejected: like a champion in the arena
like the best man in the games

choices.why: ἄτρεπτος means 'not turning, unswerving'; 'unbending' captures the firmness of the athlete's strength without importing modern athletic imagery.

νόημα is the mind's act of thinking or the thought itself; 'your thought' keeps the singular, active sense of the mental faculty opposing the labors, distinct from the broader νοῦς ('mind') used elsewhere in the work.
χάριτας ἀνάγων means 'bringing up thanks'; 'offering thanks' preserves the upward motion of ἀνάγων and the plural χάριτας as acts of gratitude.

choices.term: ἐπινεύσει γὰρ αἰτοῦντι τῷ φίλῳ τὴν χάριν
choices.english: for he will nod assent to the friend who asks for the favor
choices.why: ἐπινεύω literally means 'to nod in assent'; keeping the gesture preserves the vivid image of God granting the request, and τῷ φίλῳ ('the friend') reflects the intimate relationship between God and the believer.
rejected: for he will grant the favor to the friend who asks
for he will consent to the friend who asks

pass_b_english: Knowing these things, prepare your soul to be strong against sicknesses as well, and take courage like some excellent man in the stadiums, ready to endure hardships with unbending power. Do not let your soul be utterly crushed by grief, whether a sickness presses upon you heavily or some other difficulty befalls you. Instead, oppose your thought to the hardships with a noble spirit, offering thanks to God even in the midst of painful circumstances, since he is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover. Show mercy to those who are afflicted, and ask for God's help upon them. For he will nod assent to the friend who asks for the favor, and he will provide aid to the afflicted, wishing to make his power known to human beings, so that when they come to knowledge they may ascend to God and enjoy eternal blessedness, when the Son of God arrives restoring good things to his own people.

problems.quote: since he understands things wiser than human beings and things that people cannot easily discover.
problems.source_quote: ἅτε δὴ σοφώτερά τε ἀνθρώπων φρονοῦντι καὶ ἅπερ οὐ δυνατὸν οὐδὲ ῥᾴδιον ἀνθρώποις εὑρεῖν.
problems.why: Greek attributes wisdom to the mind (the one giving thanks), not to God; English shifts agency to God.
problems.fix: since the mind is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover.
problems.ruling: φρονοῦντι is dative agreeing with the subject offering thanks; English 'he understands' wrongly attributes wisdom to God.

edits.old: since he understands things wiser than human beings and things that people cannot easily discover.
edits.new: since the mind is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover.

fixed: Agency corrected: the Greek φρονοῦντι agrees with νόημα (the mind), not God; the English now attributes wisdom to the mind.

problems.quote: since the mind is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover
problems.source_quote: ἅτε δὴ σοφώτερά τε ἀνθρώπων φρονοῦντι καὶ ἅπερ οὐ δυνατὸν οὐδὲ ῥᾴδιον ἀνθρώποις εὑρεῖν
problems.why: The participle φρονοῦντι is dative, governed by ἀνάγων—'offering thanks to God who is wiser than humans.' English makes 'the mind' the subject.
problems.fix: offering thanks to God, who is wiser than humans and discerns what is neither possible nor easy for people to find
problems.ruling: Greek has dative φρονοῦντι referring to God (thanks to God, who thinks wiser than humans); English makes 'mind' subject and adds 'perceives' not in source.

edits.old: since the mind is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover
edits.new: since he is wiser than humans and perceives what people cannot easily discover

fixed: The source participle φρονοῦντι is dative, referring to God (the one to whom thanks are offered), not 'the mind.' Changed 'the mind' to 'he' to refer to God.
